slides.title: The Customer Voice

content.subtitle: What 12 Months of Satisfaction Data Tells Us About Where We Excel—and Where We're Losing Trust

visuals.description: Abstract visual of customer feedback/listening - speech bubbles, sound waves, or voice concept. Professional, modern, not cliché.

slides.speaker_note: This is not a data review—it's about listening to what customers are telling us through their satisfaction scores. The story: we know how to deliver excellence, but we're not doing it everywhere.

slides.title: The Performance Gap

visuals.description: Emphasize the 0.9-point gap visually - use color contrast (green for 8.1, red/amber for 7.2). Add threshold lines at 8.0 (excellence) and 7.5 (attention required).

slides.speaker_note: This is the story in one chart: Maintenance at 8.1 proves we can deliver. Breakdown at 7.2 proves we're not. That 0.9-point gap isn't data—it's customers telling us we're inconsistent.

slides.title: What Excellence Looks Like

bullets: Maintenance scores 8.1 because customers know exactly what to expect—and we deliver it
Scheduled appointments, confirmed time windows, proactive technician updates
Formula: clear communication + predictable delivery + professional execution
This isn't exceptional service—it's baseline clarity done consistently well
Proof point: we already know how to make customers happy

visuals.description: Visual metaphor for success: upward arrow, checkmarks, clear pathway, or 'blueprint' concept. Positive, confident tone.

slides.speaker_note: Maintenance is our North Star. It's not magic—it's process discipline and communication hygiene. The question isn't 'can we do this?' It's 'why aren't we doing it everywhere?'

slides.title: Where We're Losing Them

bullets: Breakdown scores 7.2 because customers are stressed and we're leaving them in the dark
Waiting for technicians, waiting for parts, waiting for updates—uncertainty compounds anxiety
Heat pumps and boilers break in winter—this isn't inconvenience, it's crisis for customers
The problem isn't technical response time. It's communication during the wait
Result: we fix the problem but lose their trust in the process

visuals.description: Visual metaphor for uncertainty/frustration: question marks, broken connection, fog/unclear path, or contrast to previous slide's clarity. Empathetic, not alarmist.

slides.speaker_note: Customers don't expect instant repairs. They expect to know what's happening. When a heat pump fails in January and we go silent, we're not just slow—we're invisible.

slides.title: The Pattern: Communication Drives Everything

bullets: High satisfaction = customers know what's happening and when it will happen
Low satisfaction = customers are uncertain about status, timeline, or next steps
Purchase journey (7.8) succeeds because onboarding sets expectations early
Customer Service (7.4) struggles not because staff are unfriendly, but because resolution feels slow and opaque
The fix isn't better products or more resources—it's transparency at every touchpoint

visuals.description: Visual diagram: communication as the connecting thread across all journeys. Could be a simple network diagram, flow concept, or 'clarity = satisfaction' visual equation.

slides.speaker_note: This is the insight that changes everything: satisfaction correlates more with communication quality than outcome quality. We don't need to be faster—we need to be clearer.

slides.title: The Path Forward

content.recommendation: Replicate Maintenance communication standards across Breakdown and Customer Service journeys—starting in 30 days
rationale: Maintenance already proves the model works: we have the blueprint, we just need to scale it
Breakdown and Customer Service fail for the same reason: customers lack visibility into progress
Communication improvements are low-cost, high-impact—no new systems, just process discipline
next_steps: Week 1-2: Deploy automated status updates for breakdown requests (ETA, technician assigned, parts status)
Week 3-4: Train customer service teams on Maintenance confirmation protocols (resolution timeline, follow-up cadence)
Month 2: Launch KTV dashboard with journey targets and weekly review rhythm
Month 3: Customer feedback sessions on heat pump and solar panel experiences to validate improvements

visuals.description: Visual roadmap or timeline showing 30-day implementation path. Progressive steps, forward momentum. Not a Gantt chart—a journey visual.

slides.speaker_note: This isn't a transformation project—it's a replication project. We know what works. Now we execute.

slides.title: Methodology

items: KTV scores: 1-10 scale, collected post-interaction (12-month rolling average)
Journeys: Maintenance, Breakdown & Repair, Purchase, Customer Service
Products: Gas boiler maintenance contracts, Heat pumps, Solar panels

slides.speaker_note: Data validated through customer feedback management system. Qualitative insights from verbatim analysis.
